THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County took up wind energy, data centers, and a potentially $60 million highway facility this week, while Wausau's Finance Committee advanced funding for a downtown development and tackled a lead service line replacement shortfall.

  • Marathon County adopted a temporary moratorium on data centers and a new battery energy storage ordinance with a 500-foot setback from all structures, then referred the Hub City Wind resolution back to the Executive Committee for a clearer recommendation at the September board meeting.
  • The Marathon County Board advanced Phase 3 of a new county highway facility that could cost up to $60 million, a significant potential commitment for county taxpayers.
  • Wausau's Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and adopted a four-session budget workshop calendar beginning October 5 at 6:30 p.m.
  • Wausau's Police & Fire Commission launched a deputy chief promotional process — applications open in September, with a decision expected at the December meeting — framed as early succession planning for the police chief role.
  • The Village of Weston Parks Committee heard a concept for a 30,000-square-foot indoor community space at Kennedy Park from Everest Youth Hockey, with no village funding committed; a public input meeting on the Mock Miller Park master plan is tentatively set for September 3rd.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation following a special meeting called for August 27.

Coming up: Wausau's Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2 at 5:30 p.m. — worth watching after a busy week of financial and policy action — and the Economic Development Committee convenes Tuesday, September 1 at 5:30 p.m. as downtown development questions remain in play.
